intro.author: Amos, a herdsman and tender of sycomore figs from Tekoa in Judah (1:1; 7:14)
intro.written: About 760 BC, 'two years before the earthquake' (1:1), in the reigns of Uzziah of Judah and Jeroboam II of Israel
intro.audience: Mainly the northern kingdom of Israel, especially its wealthy leaders in Samaria and worshipers at Bethel
intro.setting: Under Jeroboam II, Israel enjoyed peace, expanded borders and new wealth. But the prosperity was built on cheating and crushing the poor, while religious festivals at Bethel and Gilgal flourished. Amos, a southerner with no professional prophetic training, was sent north to confront it.
intro.purpose: To announce that God would judge Israel for injustice and empty worship, and that being his chosen people meant greater responsibility, not immunity.
intro.bigIdea: 'Let judgment run down as waters, and righteousness as a mighty stream' (5:24).

outline.title: Judgment on the nations, and finally on Israel
Messages against Samaria's injustice and false security
Five visions, a confrontation, and a final hope
